about: What a server does with media it serves or relays: spec/v0/media.md sections 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.2, and spec/v0/video.md sections 6.3 to 6.6, as revised by proposal 16. Generated by tools/vectors from the specification's rules.

webvtt: a part (text, or hex when it isn't UTF-8), whether it is refused, and the rebuilt part (output) when it isn't (video section 6.3). The 5 MiB part and 16 MiB track sizes and the 50,000 and 200,000 cue counts are not exercised here.
ass: the same for ASS (video section 6.4). The 5 MiB and 16 MiB sizes and the 50,000 and 200,000 event counts are not exercised here.
pgs: PGS parts, in hex, as video section 6.5 checks them; times are zero. An empty part (no hex) is valid. The 64 MiB size and 20,000 objects are not exercised here.

fonts: tiny font headers, in hex (a table directory and 4 zero bytes per table, not real fonts), as video section 6.6 checks them; type is the media type a valid font is relayed as. The 10 MiB size is not exercised here.

hls: playlists as the viewer's server checks them (media section 3.1, steps 1 to 10); reason names the step that fails first. The playback of every case has the audio tracks a1 to a40. valid means the checks pass; tags outside the subset may still be dropped before serving. The 2 MiB size and 50,000 URIs are not exercised here.

ranges: a Range header against a file of size bytes (media section 2.1): start and end, both included, when it is well-formed and satisfiable; reason says malformed or not satisfiable, both answered 416.

fileAnswers: an answer of the owning server for the file (status and headers; an absent member is an absent header), for the Range the viewer's server sent (none when absent) and the copy's size and etag from the catalog, as the viewer's server checks it (media sections 2.1, 2.3 and 3.2): valid when it relays it.

scans: the owning server's answer to a fetch under a scan ticket that has already sent sent body bytes (media section 4.2: a cap of 33,554,432 bytes): status 206 with its Content-Range, cut short at the cap, or 416 with Content-Range: bytes */<size>.

an end tag that isn't the innermost is removed; tags closed at the end
tags balanced across a cue's lines
8 open tags kept
a 9th open tag removed with its end tag
32 tags on a line kept
a 33rd tag on a line removed
a line of tags alone is dropped with its tags
spaces collapsed across tags, written where the run starts
spaces at the end removed, tags after them or not
an unknown tag
a tag without its >

a lone < stays, escaped

a bad first setting of a name: the second is dropped too

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:02.000 region:r1 vertical:rl foo:bar line	size:10% position:20%

a malformed timing: the block dropped
a timing without spaces around -->: the block dropped
4 digits of hours: the block dropped
a cue left empty: dropped
a line shaped like a timing, inside a cue, is text
a cue right after the header, without an empty line
a line of spaces doesn't end a block
out-of-range timings are not checked
a line of 500 bytes kept whole
a line cut to 500 bytes, not splitting a character
tags don't count in the 500 bytes; tags past the cut removed
a cut at a space: the space removed
escaping comes after the cut
no cue left: valid
the header is a prefix
no WEBVTT header
empty
